div.p:
I swear by Apollo the physician, and Asclepius, and Hygieia, and Panacea, and all the gods and goddesses, making them my witnesses, that I will fulfill according to my ability and judgment this oath and this covenant: to hold him who taught me this art as equal to my parents, to share my livelihood with him, to give him a share when he is in need of money, to regard his offspring as equal to my brothers in male lineage, and to teach them this art, if they wish to learn it, without fee and covenant; to impart precept, oral instruction, and all the rest of the learning to my sons, to the sons of him who taught me, and to indentured pupils who have sworn the physician's oath, but to no one else. I will use dietary regimens for the benefit of the sick according to my ability and judgment, and keep them from harm and injustice. I will neither give a deadly drug to anyone if asked for it, nor suggest such counsel; likewise I will not give a woman a destructive pessary. In purity and holiness I will guard my life and my art. I will not cut, not even those suffering from stone, but will leave this to men who are practitioners of this work.
Into whatever houses I enter, I will go for the benefit of the sick, abstaining from every voluntary injustice and corruption, especially sexual acts upon the bodies of women and men, both free and slave. Whatever I see or hear in the course of treatment, or even outside treatment in the life of men, that ought never to be spoken abroad, I will keep silent, holding such things to be unspoken secrets. If I fulfill this oath and do not violate it, may it be granted to me to enjoy both life and art, honored among all men for all time; but if I transgress and swear falsely, may the opposite of these things befall me.
